corpus.corpus_title: Lithium Dendrite Formation and Suppression in All-Solid-State Electrolytes

findings.claim: In situ microscopy shows Li nucleates and propagates directly inside sulfide solid electrolytes (Li3PS4), causing structural cracking, linked to P- and S-based crystalline defects.

In Li-In anode full cells with sulfide electrolyte (Li6PS5Cl) at high loading and rate, Li-In dendrites grow enclosing electrolyte particles, causing cell death; STEM-EELS and DFT reveal the mechanism.
Dendrites form inside the bulk of inorganic solid-state electrolytes despite their mechanical strength, and dendrite growth models within SSEs and suppression strategies are reviewed.
In garnet LLZO single crystals, dendrite tips are accompanied by dislocations, suggesting dendrite-induced stress generates dislocations that influence electrolyte fracture.

Crystalline grain boundaries and bulk/surface defects in garnet LLZO facilitate filament growth; amorphous LLZO with no grain boundaries blocks penetration up to 3.2 mA/cm2 and enables thin-film microbatteries cycled over 500 times at 10C.

Interfacial void growth during Li dissolution precedes dendrite nucleation in garnet electrolytes; void edges can amplify current density by up to four orders of magnitude, and low-solubility metallic interlayers delay void growth.
Buffer layers between Li metal and solid electrolyte stabilize electrodeposition; modeling predicts Ag, Al, Sn, and Li3S(BF4)0.5Cl0.5 are effective buffers.
A liquid-metal-loaded molecular sieve filler in PEO polymer electrolyte improves ionic conductivity and blocks dendrites, giving more uniform Li deposition.
A Li2CO3-Li3BO3-Li2SO4 glass-ceramic electrolyte, stable against Li, reached 2e-5 S/cm at room temperature with ASR below 30 ohm cm2 and showed dendrite-free symmetric cycling in glass form.

open_gaps: No unified quantitative criterion linking defect density, grain boundaries, and voids to the critical current density at which dendrites nucleate inside sulfide and oxide electrolytes.
Operando observation of dendrite growth inside sulfide electrolytes under realistic stack pressure and high areal capacity is largely missing.
Buffer predictions from modeling (Ag, Al, Sn) lack broad experimental validation across electrolyte chemistries.
Dislocation generation mechanism by dendrite stress in ceramics is speculative and not yet quantified.
Polymer and glass-ceramic dendrite-blocking routes have limited data on conductivity-versus-dendrite-tolerance tradeoffs at practical thickness and temperature.
